analysis: Integration across all seven batch analyses. The PR is mostly CHANGELOG.md documentation, plus a provider lifecycle reliability change. The code changes are LaunchAgent.restartAfterDrain, which now polls isLoaded for up to 60s before bootstrapping, and a new ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider, which re-arms the watchdog via defer on both success and failure. RestartCommand and UpdateCommand use the new helper. LaunchctlControl adds task-local test seams (runnerForTesting, homeDirectoryForTesting) and a homeDirectory() helper used by plistPath() and logPath(). I did not see the LaunchctlControl source, so I could not confirm that homeDirectory() resolves from the passwd entry rather than environment variables. The operator already controls the machine under TB-003, so any impact would be low and I could not show a concrete issue. The test seams are task-local with no environment or file-based activation, so production cannot bind them and they add no attack surface. The watchdog re-arm (T-043) restores crash recovery after a failed relaunch and does not add rollback authority. kickstartIfLoaded acts only on a loaded job. In UpdateCommand the watchdog is re-armed before cancelPendingCandidateAttempt in the catch path. This is a speculative ordering window, and the updater and watchdog internals were not visible. loadService re-enables the job, which could override a concurrent `darkbloom stop` during the wait. That behavior is pre-existing and presumably covered by the drain lease, which was not supplied. The changelog text is consistent with the canonical T-041 (30-minute TTL, 20 GiB reserve), TB-011/T-052..T-058 and T-031 closure. No threat-model assumption is invalidated and I found no new attack surface that can be shown. Coverage limits: the changelog patch hunks were not always visible, and the watchdog, updater and LaunchctlControl.homeDirectory implementation were not supplied. A later pass with that source should check the home-directory resolution, the watchdog/pending-candidate ordering, and the stop/drain lease interaction.
